I need to decide on an auction bid for Reading Railroad.

The current bid is $250 by p2. I have no monopolies and $1012 cash. I will bid $251 to win the auction.

Reading Railroad is 25% over its $200 list price. I will bid $251 to win the auction.

A $251 bid leaves $761 cash, which covers the $480 needed for Marvin and New York. I am weighing whether to drop out instead, since p2 already holds two railroads and would gain another at $250, while p1 might bid higher if I withdraw.

Denying p2 a second railroad is valuable because p2 is the most dangerous opponent. I will bid $251.

I am reconsidering the $251 bid. Both p1 and p2 want Reading Railroad to complete their sets, so they will likely raise again. I could cap the auction at $255 or $260, but the pattern suggests a war above my $260 limit.

I am now considering dropping out. p2 only has $686, so a high bid would drain their cash and reduce their threat. I own Park Place, which blocks them from completing dark blue. p1 has $1033 and can afford any bid.

p2 cannot complete any color set without trading or buying several unowned properties. p1 also lacks a complete set, as his light blue and orange paths are blocked by my holdings.

No player currently holds a color monopoly. A second railroad would raise rent from $25 to $50 per landing, which is a meaningful income boost.

Standard strategy suggests not overpaying for a single railroad when a full set is hard to complete. B&O remains unowned, so I could still acquire a second railroad later. Buying Reading now would leave $761 cash. That covers B&O plus Marvin and New York, though the total is tight.

I am now leaning toward bidding $255 or $260 as a final offer within my cap. A $251 bid would invite another round and pressure me to exceed my limit. I will make the public message firm but avoid telegraphing that this is my last bid, since p2 has already shown they want the pair.

I will bid $251 to force a higher bid. If the opponent exceeds my cap, I will drop and drain their cash. If both drop at my bid, I win for $251, which is acceptable.

I will bid $255. That is a small increase over $251, but it may make p1 hesitate. p2 has only $686 cash and would be left with roughly $426 if he pays above $260.
